text: I just had a tooth extracted yesterday. I had tooth sensitivity for about two weeks, but I thought it was just a simple cavity, so I went to a clinic in another province to get a filling. After the dentist examined me, they recommended extraction because the cavity was deep and a filling probably wouldn't hold. But I'm afraid of needles and tooth extraction, so I insisted on getting a filling first. The dentist filled it but warned me that if I still had pain or sensitivity after a month, I should get it extracted. Before filling, the dentist asked if I wanted local anesthesia, and I said no. It was very sensitive during the procedure, and afterward, it hurt a lot for about three hours. Even paracetamol didn't help. About 1-2 weeks later, I started having pain in the same tooth that had been filled, so I decided to have it extracted at this clinic because I'd seen good reviews. Honestly, I was terrified before the extraction. The staff checked my blood pressure twice because my heart was beating fast. After the examination and X-rays, the dentist said the tooth was decayed. I decided to have it extracted. The dentist injected local anesthesia, and I didn't feel any pain. I waited 10 minutes for the anesthesia to take effect. Then, the dentist extracted the tooth in 10 seconds – it was very quick and easy. I was still wondering if it was over already; it was so fast! The dentist was great, and the staff were polite and provided good service. They also gave me a post-extraction instruction sheet. Having a tooth extracted at this clinic wasn't as scary as I thought. When I got home, the anesthetic was wearing off, so I ate some meatballs. After the anesthetic wore off, I didn't feel any pain at all. Now I just have to wait for the wound to heal.
